chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I was in the presence of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and a man came to him and said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad! I am afflicted with women, so I commit adultery one day and fast one day, so that one becomes expiation for the other.' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'There is nothing more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than that He is obeyed and not disobeyed. Therefore, do not commit adultery and do not fast.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) pulled him towards him, took his hand, and said, 'O Abu Zannah (Father of Adultery)! You are doing the deed of the inhabitants of the Fire and you hope that you will enter Paradise?'

key_terms.أَبَا زَنَّةَ: O Father of Adultery (nickname used by the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Does fasting one day and committing adultery the next serve as expiation for sins in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) corrects the common misconception of ritualistic compensation by emphasizing that true piety requires consistent obedience rather than alternating sin with worship. The subsequent intervention by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unity of action and intention, warning that mechanical ritual without moral integrity leads to spiritual ruin. This narrative illustrates the principle that good deeds do not cancel out major sins unless accompanied by genuine repentance and consistent practice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘I was in the presence of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, so a man came over and said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! I am afflicted (addicted) with the women, so I commit adultery one day, and I Fast one day. So, does that become an expiation for that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘There is nothing more Beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic than that He<sup>azwj</sup> is obeyed and is not disobeyed. Therefore, do not commit adultery and do not Fast (as an expiation for it)’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> pulled him and grabbed his hand and said: ‘O father of adultery! You are doing a deed of the inhabitants of the Fire and you are hoping that you would enter the Paradise?’
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“Once I was with Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a man came and said, ‘O abu Muhammad, I am addicted to women. One day I commit fornication and the other day I fast; if this can become expiation for the sin.’ Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘There is not anything more beloved to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, than obedience to Him and not to disobey Him. So you must not fornicate and you must not fast.’ Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, pulled him to himself holding his hand and said, ‘O fornicator, you do the deeds of the people of hell and hope to enter paradise?”’
